# Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR)

> FCR lets rollups, bridges, exchanges and apps accept deposits and messages from Ethereum in as little as 24 seconds, backed by Ethereum's validator set. It is a consensus-client feature: no hard fork, no new contracts. Instead of waiting for finality (~13 minutes) or counting a fixed number of blocks, FCR counts validator attestations and marks a block fast-confirmed once enough of them support it. Integrators read the `safe` block tag instead of `finalized`.

Key facts:

- Speed: at minimum 24 seconds for FCR to confirm a block; a bridge adds its own steps on top. Finality takes ~13 minutes.
- Security: FCR checks that validators keep the block in the chain, under stated assumptions about adversarial stake and network synchrony. If those fail, a fast-confirmed block can reorg; integrators re-check once the block is finalized.
- Evidence: a research paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00549), a Lean 4 formal safety proof (https://github.com/fradamt/verified-fast-confirmation), in scope of the Ethereum Foundation bug bounty, and a one-year replay of mainnet through the clients' FCR code with 0 false confirmations (2.56M slots; no fast-confirmed block was reorged).
- Client support: shipped in Lighthouse, Prysm, Nimbus (on by default) and Lodestar; experimental in Teku.
- RPC providers that serve FCR: Alchemy, Chainstack, Quicknode and Tenderly.
- In production: Gnosis Chain has used FCR for deposits from Ethereum since 7 October 2026 (its bridges wait for FCR instead of finality, ~13 minutes). Chainlink CCIP 2.0 has it live on testnet.
- Developed by Ethlabs, the Ethereum Foundation and Ethereum's consensus-client teams.

- [Quick start](https://fastconfirm.it/docs/integrate/quick-start): the one-line change and how to turn FCR on
- [How it works](https://fastconfirm.it/docs/evaluate/how-it-works): the rule, step by step
- [Assumptions and attacks](https://fastconfirm.it/docs/evaluate/assumptions-and-attacks): what FCR relies on and how it could fail
- [Security](https://fastconfirm.it/docs/evaluate/security): the safety argument, the formal proof and the bug bounty
- [Comparison](https://fastconfirm.it/docs/evaluate/comparison): FCR against finality and k-block waits
